message.abstract: <jats:p>Accurate short-term wind power forecasting is essential for wind farm operation and grid dispatch, but remains challenging for newly constructed wind farms in complex terrain due to limited turbine-level data and heterogeneous flow responses. Online computational fluid dynamics (CFD) can capture terrain-induced flow variability, but is too costly for routine forecasting. This study proposes a physics-guided farm-scale power forecasting approach that combines precomputed CFD-derived spatial priors, numerical weather prediction (NWP)-guided temporal forecasting, and physically constrained power conversion. Offline CFD simulations are grouped by wind direction and atmospheric stability to construct spatial priors for turbine-level inflow differences in complex terrain. A residual temporal network extracts temporal inflow features from meteorological mast observations and NWP predictors. These temporal features are fused with the CFD-derived spatial priors to infer turbine-level wind speed, which is then converted into power via a physical power curve model. The physical curve is calibrated using limited initial supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) data under a low-dimensional maximum a posteriori formulation. Validation at the Oya wind farm in South Africa shows that, compared with a baseline without CFD priors and curve calibration, the proposed approach reduces farm-level normalized RMSE from 16.37% to 11.96% and normalized MAE from 10.59% to 6.33%. It also outperforms empirical, neural network, and tree-based approaches under the same data-limited setting. The results demonstrate a physically interpretable and computationally efficient solution for short-term power forecasting in complex terrain.</jats:p>
title: Short-term wind power forecasting for data-limited wind farms in complex terrain: A physics-guided approach with CFD-derived spatial priors
